1) Core plugin structure and rule registry (REQ-PLUGIN-STRUCTURE, REQ-RULE-REGISTRY, REQ-TYPESCRIPT, REQ-NPM-PACKAGE): - src/index.ts (TypeScript) is the plugin entry point and is annotated: /** * ESLint Traceability Plugin * @story docs/stories/001.0-DEV-PLUGIN-SETUP.story.md * @req REQ-PLUGIN-STRUCTURE - Provide foundational plugin export and registration * @req REQ-ERROR-HANDLING - Gracefully handles plugin loading errors and missing dependencies */ - Dynamic rule registry: - const RULE_NAMES = ["require-story-annotation", "require-req-annotation", "require-branch-annotation", "valid-annotation-format", "valid-story-reference", "valid-req-reference"] as const; - const rules: Record = {} as any; - RULE_NAMES.forEach((name) => { const mod = require(`./rules/${name}`); rules[name] = mod.default ?? mod; ... }); - Rules implemented in TypeScript: - src/rules/require-story-annotation.ts - src/rules/require-req-annotation.ts - src/rules/require-branch-annotation.ts - src/rules/valid-annotation-format.ts - src/rules/valid-story-reference.ts - src/rules/valid-req-reference.ts - NPM package structure (REQ-NPM-PACKAGE): - package.json: - "name": "eslint-plugin-traceability" - "main": "lib/src/index.js" - "types": "lib/src/index.d.ts" - "files": ["lib", "README.md", "LICENSE"] - "peerDependencies": { "eslint": "^9.0.0" } - "engines": { "node": ">=18.18.0" }
2) Error handling for rule loading (REQ-ERROR-HANDLING, acceptance criterion: Error Handling): - src/index.ts wraps dynamic rule loading in try/catch: - On failure: - console.error(`[eslint-plugin-traceability] Failed to load rule "${name}": ${error.message}`); - Installs a placeholder RuleModule whose create() reports an ESLint error: - message: `eslint-plugin-traceability: Error loading rule "${name}": ${error.message}` - Behavior verified in tests/plugin-setup-error.test.ts (explicitly tied to this story): - File header: - @story docs/stories/001.0-DEV-PLUGIN-SETUP.story.md - @req REQ-ERROR-HANDLING - Gracefully handles plugin loading errors and missing dependencies - Test: - Mocks ../src/rules/require-branch-annotation to throw new Error("Test load error"); - Requires ../src/index; - Asserts: - console.error called with string containing 'Failed to load rule "require-branch-annotation": Test load error'; - plugin.rules["require-branch-annotation"] is defined; - placeholderRule.meta.docs.description contains "Failed to load rule 'require-branch-annotation'"; - placeholderRule.create(fakeContext).Program(...) calls context.report with message containing 'Error loading rule "require-branch-annotation": Test load error'. - Additional CLI-level error handling coverage in tests/cli-error-handling.test.ts: - Header: - @story docs/stories/001.0-DEV-PLUGIN-SETUP.story.md - @req REQ-ERROR-HANDLING - Plugin CLI should exit with error on rule load failure - Uses child_process.spawnSync to run ESLint CLI with this plugin and asserts non-zero exit plus expected error output.
3) Core plugin registration and load (Acceptance: Core Functionality, REQ-PLUGIN-STRUCTURE, REQ-TEST-SETUP): - src/index.ts exports plugin components: - const configs = { recommended: [createTraceabilityFlatConfig()], strict: [createTraceabilityFlatConfig()] }; - export { rules, configs, maintenance }; - export default { rules, configs, maintenance }; - tests/plugin-setup.test.ts validates basic exports: - Header: - @story docs/stories/001.0-DEV-PLUGIN-SETUP.story.md - @req REQ-PLUGIN-STRUCTURE - plugin exports rules and configs - Imports plugin, { rules, configs } from "../src/index"; - Test asserts: - rules and configs are defined and typeof === "object"; - plugin.rules === rules and plugin.configs === configs; - This ensures the plugin module loads without errors and exposes the expected shape. - Jest configuration (jest.config.js) provides the test infrastructure (REQ-TEST-SETUP) with ts-jest and Node test environment, collecting coverage for src/**/* and ignoring lib/.
4) ESLint v9 flat config integration (Acceptance: Integration, REQ-ESLINT-COMPAT): - Flat config supplied by plugin (src/index.ts): - createTraceabilityFlatConfig() returns: - { plugins: { traceability: {} }, rules: { ...TRACEABILITY_RULE_SEVERITIES } } - configs object: - { recommended: [createTraceabilityFlatConfig()], strict: [createTraceabilityFlatConfig()] } - This matches ESLint v9 flat config expectations (array of plain config objects with plugins and rules). - CLI integration test using ESLint v9 CLI and flat config: - tests/integration/cli-integration.test.ts: - Header: - @story docs/stories/001.0-DEV-PLUGIN-SETUP.story.md - @req REQ-PLUGIN-STRUCTURE - Validate plugin registers via CLI - Resolves ESLint CLI from eslint/package.json and uses tests/eslint.config.js via --config. - For multiple test cases, it: - Passes code snippets via --stdin; - Sets flat-config rules such as "traceability/require-story-annotation:error" and "traceability/require-req-annotation:error"; - Asserts result.status equals expectedStatus (0 or 1), verifying that rules load and run correctly through ESLint v9 flat config. - Additional configuration and integration guidance in user-docs/eslint-9-setup-guide.md: - Example: - import js from "@eslint/js"; - import traceability from "eslint-plugin-traceability"; - export default [js.configs.recommended, traceability.configs.recommended]; - Complete working example for a TypeScript plugin project with flat config, showing conditional import of the built plugin.
5) User experience: installation and configuration instructions (Acceptance: User Experience, REQ-NPM-PACKAGE, REQ-ESLINT-COMPAT): - README.md: - Installation: - npm install --save-dev eslint-plugin-traceability - yarn add --dev eslint-plugin-traceability - Basic CommonJS flat config example (plugins: { traceability: {} }, rules: { "traceability/require-story-annotation": "error", ... }). - Quick Start shows ESM flat config using plugin presets: - import traceability from "eslint-plugin-traceability"; - export default [traceability.configs.recommended]; - Lists available rules and links to docs/rules/*.md for each rule. - Points users to user-docs/eslint-9-setup-guide.md, user-docs/api-reference.md, and user-docs/examples.md for extended documentation and troubleshooting. - Package.json confirms publishable plugin structure (main/types/files, peerDependencies on ESLint, engines for Node), satisfying REQ-NPM-PACKAGE.
6) Documentation of plugin structure and development setup (Acceptance: Documentation, Quality Standards): - docs/eslint-plugin-development-guide.md: - Explains plugin object shape (meta, configs, rules, processors) and provides a template for src/index.ts. - Describes meta data best practices, reading from package.json, rule structure, configuration presets (recommended/strict), and how to use them in eslint.config.js. - Gives TypeScript-specific guidance, RuleTester usage, and testing strategy (unit, integration, filesystem tests). - Includes build & distribution setup (tsconfig, package.json) and recommended linting for the plugin project itself. - user-docs/eslint-9-setup-guide.md: - Comprehensive ESLint 9 flat config guide with examples for JS, TS, mixed projects, tests, monorepos, and plugin development. - Shows direct integration of eslint-plugin-traceability via traceability.configs.recommended in an ESLint 9 flat config. - README.md ties together installation, configuration, rule docs, and extended guides, providing a clear onboarding path.
7) Targeted tests execution (via assessment tools): - Command run during assessment: - npm test -- --runInBand --verbose tests/plugin-setup.test.ts tests/plugin-setup-error.test.ts tests/cli-error-handling.test.ts - Reported Jest command: - jest --ci --bail --runInBand --verbose tests/plugin-setup.test.ts tests/plugin-setup-error.test.ts tests/cli-error-handling.test.ts - No error or stack trace output was emitted, indicating these story-specific tests executed without reported failures, supporting that the plugin loads, exports, and handles rule-load errors as specified.
traceability.notes:
The story docs/stories/001.0-DEV-PLUGIN-SETUP.story.md defines the foundational ESLint plugin structure, including plugin registration, compatibility with ESLint v9 flat config, error handling, test setup, npm packaging, and documentation. The implementation in this repository fulfills these requirements:
- Core Functionality and Plugin Structure: src/index.ts defines the plugin in TypeScript, dynamically registers all traceability rules, and exports rules and flat-config presets (recommended/strict). tests/plugin-setup.test.ts verifies that the default export and named exports (rules, configs) are present and correctly wired. - Error Handling: Dynamic rule loading is wrapped in try/catch with clear console.error logging and a placeholder rule that reports a specific ESLint error when loading fails. tests/plugin-setup-error.test.ts and tests/cli-error-handling.test.ts (both tagged to this story) confirm this behavior at module level and via the ESLint CLI. - ESLint v9 Flat Config Integration: The plugin exposes flat-config presets, and tests/integration/cli-integration.test.ts uses ESLint’s CLI with a flat eslint.config.js to run multiple traceability rules, asserting correct exit codes. user-docs/eslint-9-setup-guide.md and README.md provide concrete examples of wiring the plugin into ESLint 9 flat configs. - User Experience: README.md documents installation, configuration (both direct rule usage and preset-based), and links to further user and developer documentation. Package.json is correctly structured as a publishable ESLint plugin with appropriate main/types, files, peerDependencies, and engines. - Testing Infrastructure and Documentation: jest.config.js (with ts-jest), multiple targeted tests tied to this story, docs/eslint-plugin-development-guide.md, and user-docs/eslint-9-setup-guide.md collectively provide a solid test and development setup.
Given this concrete evidence across code, tests, and documentation, all acceptance criteria and listed requirements for 001.0-DEV-PLUGIN-SETUP are satisfied, so the story is assessed as PASSED.
